model_claims.text: The PR wraps urllib3.exceptions.LocationParseError raised from urllib3.util.connection.create_connection in requests.exceptions.InvalidURL so callers see a requests-native exception instead of a raw urllib3 one.
model_claims.source_quote: Wrap `urllib3.exceptions.LocationParseError` raised from inside `urllib3.util.connection.create_connection` in `requests.exceptions.InvalidURL`, so callers see a requests-native exception instead of a raw urllib3 one.

model_claims.text: The existing (`_SSLError`, `_HTTPError`) except clause in HTTPAdapter.send catches LocationParseError but then re‑raises it bare via the trailing else clause.
model_claims.source_quote: The `(_SSLError, _HTTPError)` `except` clause in `HTTPAdapter.send` does catch it — `LocationParseError` is a `urllib3.exceptions.HTTPError` — but falls through to the trailing `else: raise` and re-raises it bare.

model_claims.text: The fix adds an explicit isinstance check for LocationParseError (referred to as LocationValueError) that wraps it in InvalidURL, mirroring the existing handling elsewhere in the method.
model_claims.source_quote: The fix adds an explicit `isinstance(e, LocationValueError)` branch that wraps it in `InvalidURL`, mirroring the behaviour of `get_connection_with_tls_context` earlier in the same method.

model_claims.text: Before the fix, requesting a URL with a label longer than 63 characters causes urllib3.exceptions.LocationParseError to leak out of requests.get.
model_claims.source_quote: # BEFORE — on origin/main, the urllib3 exception leaks.

model_claims.text: After applying the fix, the same request raises requests.exceptions.InvalidURL instead of leaking the urllib3 exception.
model_claims.source_quote: # AFTER — checkout this PR's branch and re-run the exact same script.

model_claims.text: For a URL with a label longer than 63 characters, the PR changes the leaked urllib3.exceptions.LocationParseError into a requests.exceptions.InvalidURL.
For a URL containing a wildcard (*) the behavior remains InvalidURL both before and after the PR.
For a zone‑id‑less IPv6 URL the behavior remains InvalidURL both before and after the PR.
For a normal URL that results in a connect timeout, the behavior remains ConnectTimeout both before and after the PR.
For a normal URL that results in a protocol error, the behavior remains ConnectionError both before and after the PR.
model_claims.source_quote: | Normal URL → `ProtocolError` | `ConnectionError` | `ConnectionError` (unchanged) | dedicated `(ProtocolError, OSError)` branch still catches |

model_claims.text: For a normal URL that triggers an urllib3 _InvalidHeader error, the behavior remains InvalidHeader both before and after the PR.
model_claims.source_quote: | Normal URL → urllib3 `_InvalidHeader` | `InvalidHeader` | `InvalidHeader` (unchanged) | branch ordered before the new one |
